newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Dec electricity ends lower in dull session.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Dec electricity ends lower in dull session.

text.p: NYMEX December electricity futures settled lower Monday in a very dull session, reflecting lackluster activity in both physical and over-the-counter western power markets.
"People are out. It's been a busy couple of weeks here," said one Houston trader.
Overall participation was thin today due to holiday observances in U.S. and Canada.
"There was no daily trading, no clear direction from gas," the trader noted.
Softer natural gas prices in the West underpinned the complex's weakness late last week. Today's activity in the natgas market was too lackluster.

December California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled down 13 cents at $23.45 a megawatt hour (MWh). January 1997 COB finished down 19 cents at $20.70. Other COB contracts were most flat from Friday's close.
December Palo Verde (PV) futures ended down 35 cents at $21.40. January 1997 PV settled down 17 cents at $19.33. Most deferred PV months were inactive.
Most brokers and traders expected the electricity complex to be pressured by mild weather in the most of the western U.S.
"It's very neutral right now. It's not going to be as warm as it was last week," said another Houston trader.
He noted daily peak temperatures in the Pacific Northwest were expected to hit the mid-50s Fahrenheit this week, rather than in the low-60s.
